Cash flow not entered: filing discloses only six-month cumulative cash flow, not the quarter in isolation. Segment reporting (Banking/Treasury/Property-Investments, p.15) is also six-month only, not quarter-only. Company basis = Bank standalone (unconsolidated, no Seylan Developments PLC subsidiary).

interim_updates.note_text: Seylan Bank posted Group Total Operating Income of Rs.13.29bn for Q2 2026 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 14% YoY, with PAT up 16% (Rs.2.78bn to Rs.3.23bn). For H1 2026 (six months), the Bank reported PAT of Rs.6.08bn, up 10.78% YoY, with total assets reaching Rs.976bn (+19% YoY from Rs.812bn a year earlier). Per the Bank's own H1 commentary, net interest income grew 10.12% but Net Interest Margin compressed from 4.50% to 4.16% as the balance sheet grew faster than net interest income; net fee-based income grew a stronger 20.85% on Cards, Remittances, Trade and Loans fee income. H1 impairment charges rose 74.98% YoY (Rs.419mn to Rs.733mn). Return on Equity fell from 15.89% to 14.74% and Return on Assets (pre-tax) fell from 2.31% to 1.98% -- profit grew but the balance sheet grew faster, the same dynamic seen in UB Finance's Q1 filing this same period. Cost-to-Income ratio also worsened from 44.52% to 48.09%. Capital ratios softened (Total Capital Ratio 17.89% to 15.56%; CET1 12.39% to 10.91%), partly explained by the maturity and redemption of a Rs.6.0bn Basel III Tier 2 subordinated debenture on 11 April 2026 (per note 6.3), which reduced the Bank's Tier 2 capital base -- still comfortably above all regulatory minimums, and asset quality held steady (net Stage 3 impaired loans ratio flat at 1.03%, one of the highest provision cover ratios in the industry at 85.26%).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one (e.g. 31 March 2026) has been collected for SEYB -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Cash flow and segment reporting in this filing are six-month cumulative only, not quarter-isolated, so they are not entered into financial_statements and the segment commentary above (Banking/Treasury/Property-Investments) reflects H1 2026, not the quarter alone.
interim_updates.takeaway: Solid, broad-based profit growth (PAT +10.78% H1, +16.37% for the quarter alone) but three genuine quality-of-earnings caveats disclosed by the Bank itself: NIM compression, a worsening cost-to-income ratio, and declining ROE/ROA despite rising absolute profit -- the balance sheet is growing faster than earnings. The capital-ratio softening has a clean, one-off explanation (a Rs.6bn Tier 2 debenture redemption in April 2026), not a deterioration in underlying capital generation, and asset quality (Stage 3 ratio, provision cover) remains a genuine strength.
operational_highlights: Group Total Operating Income Rs.13.29bn for the quarter, up 14% YoY; PAT Rs.3.23bn, up 16% YoY
H1 2026: PAT Rs.6.08bn (+10.78% YoY), PBT Rs.9.30bn (+10.10% YoY), total assets Rs.976bn (+19% YoY from Rs.812bn a year earlier)
Net Interest Margin compressed from 4.50% to 4.16% H1 YoY despite Net Interest Income growing 10.12%, as balance sheet growth outpaced NII growth
H1 impairment charges rose 74.98% YoY (Rs.419mn to Rs.733mn)
Return on Equity fell from 15.89% to 14.74%; Return on Assets (pre-tax) fell from 2.31% to 1.98%; Cost-to-Income ratio worsened from 44.52% to 48.09%

Capital ratios softened (Total Capital Ratio 17.89% to 15.56%) mainly due to the redemption of a Rs.6.0bn Basel III Tier 2 subordinated debenture on 11 April 2026 (a one-off, not an earnings issue) -- still well above regulatory minimums
Asset quality held steady: net Stage 3 (impaired loans) ratio flat at 1.03%, gross ratio improved (7.54% to 6.97%), Stage 3 provision cover 85.26%, one of the highest in the industry
key_drivers: Net interest income growth (10.12% H1 YoY) was driven by balance sheet growth (loans and advances Rs.600bn to Rs.650bn, deposits Rs.733bn to Rs.771bn over H1 2026 alone) rather than margin expansion -- NIM actually compressed 34bps

Net fee-based income growth (20.85% H1 YoY) outpaced net interest income growth, driven by Cards, Remittances, Trade and Loans fee income per the Bank's own commentary -- a genuinely diversifying revenue mix

The Rs.6.0bn Tier 2 debenture redemption (11 April 2026, see note 6.3 and the separate Debentures schedule p.17) is the specific, disclosed cause of the capital-ratio decline -- distinguishable from any deterioration in retained-earnings-driven capital generation

Impairment charges nearly doubling H1 YoY (+74.98%) despite a stable/improving Stage 3 ratio suggests forward-looking provisioning (the Bank cites Ditwah Cyclone and Middle East Crisis management overlays in note 6.1) rather than realized credit deterioration
